message.content:
**Kill Visual Studio Code (code.exe) from the command line** | What you want | Command | Notes | |---------------|---------|-------| | **Terminate all VS Code processes (including child processes)** | ```cmd
taskkill /IM code.exe /F /T
``` | `/IM` – match by image name.
`/F` – force termination.
`/T` – terminate child processes spawned by the main process. | | **Terminate only the main VS Code process** | ```cmd
taskkill /IM code.exe /F
``` | Leaves any child processes (e.g., extensions) running. | | **Terminate a specific instance by PID** | ```cmd
taskkill /PID /F
``` | Replace `` with the number shown by `tasklist`. | --- ### Quick steps 1. **Open a Command Prompt (or PowerShell).** *Press `Win + R`, type `cmd`, hit Enter.* 2. **List running VS Code processes (optional).** ```cmd tasklist /FI "IMAGENAME eq code.exe" ``` This shows the PIDs of all `code.exe` instances. 3. **Kill them.** *To kill everything:* ```cmd taskkill /IM code.exe /F /T ``` *To kill just the main process:* ```cmd taskkill /IM code.exe /F ``` --- ### Alternative: PowerShell ```powershell # Kill all VS Code processes Get-Process code | Stop-Process -Force # Or kill by name (same effect) Stop-Process -Name code -Force ``` --- ### Why use `/T`? VS Code spawns several helper processes (`code.exe` child processes) for extensions, debugging, etc. `/T` ensures those helpers are also terminated; otherwise, they may linger after the main window closes. --- ### Caution - **Forceful termination** (`/F`) may cause unsaved work to be lost. - If you only want to close the UI but keep background tasks, use the normal “Close” button or `Ctrl‑W`/`Ctrl‑Q` instead of `taskkill`. That’s it—just run the appropriate `taskkill` command and VS Code will shut down.
